earlier_scan.source_named: Nissim, Gabriel M. 1981. Le bamileke-ghomala' (parler de Bandjoun, Cameroun): phonologie, morphologie. Paris: SELAF; not online-reachable

sources.citation: Rolle, Nicholas. 2025. A tonological rarity: Tone-driven epenthesis in Ghomala'. In N. Kuznetsova, C. Anderson & S. Easterday (eds.), Rarities in phonetics and phonology (Language Science Press, ch. 9, pp. 359ff). DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15148178
sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'Phonological profile' gives segment inventory, codas /m ŋ p k ʔ/, monosyllabic roots and a six-way tone contrast (H, ꜜH, L°, L, LH, HL; after Nissim 1981:150,153); nothing at all on word stress or accent.

sources.citation: Kamdem, Eliane Sonkoue Meli Epse. 2020. Tense-Aspect Categories and Standard Negation in Five Bamileke Languages of Cameroon: A Descriptive and Comparative Study. PhD dissertation, University of Bayreuth.
sources.note: Covers Ghomala' among five Bamileke languages; discusses tone and syllable structure of verb roots only; zero occurrences of 'stress'/'accent' in the linguistic sense.

sources.citation: Bessala, Gaston & Francine Moguo. 2017. The conditional mood in Ghomálá'. Studies in African Linguistics 46(1-2): 143-156.

sources.citation: Watters, John R. 2003. Grassfields Bantu. In Nurse & Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 225-256. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Mentions Banjoun (Ghomala') for vowels, consonants, noun classes and verb suffixes (citing Nissim 1981) but has no statement on stress/accent for Ghomala' or for Grassfields generally.

sources.citation: Mba, Gabriel. 1996/97. Les extensions verbales en ghɔmálá'. Journal of West African Languages 26(1): 77-101.
sources.note: Image-only scan; scanned of pp. 1-5 : verbs split into high-tone and low-tone classes, consonant alternation; no mention of accent.

sources.citation: Boyd, Raymond. 1989. Tone feature analysis: applications to Grassfields Bantu languages (section 2: Ghomala' Bamileke, data from Nissim 1981). HAL hal-00342650.
sources.note: Feature-based tone derivations for Ghomala' associative constructions; no stress/accent statement.
